summary: Iteration 26 testing — email verification magic-link, company + BGV verification, admin approval, verified badges, and custom project template. 16/16 backend tests pass. Frontend flows mostly pass; one critical bug found in VerifyEmail.jsx where React StrictMode causes the /auth/verify-email endpoint to be called twice, consuming the token on the first call and returning 400 on the second — so the UI always displays the error state even after a successful verification. Also, the TalentDashboard 'companies-hiring' section shows only top-12 employers sorted by hours_balance, so the only currently-verified employer (TestCo, hours=0) is never rendered — golden-star badge is code-correct but not visible with current data.

ui_bugs.issue: useEffect fires twice under React.StrictMode (index.js), so the magic-link token is consumed on the first request and the second call returns 400 -> UI ends up in the 'fail' state and shows verify-email-error even though verification actually succeeded on the server. Add a useRef guard (e.g. `const called = useRef(false); if (called.current) return; called.current = true;`) or drop StrictMode double-invocation for this effect. Currently every real user completing the magic-link flow sees a 'Link expired' screen.

The section only renders top-12 employers sorted by (-hours_balance, -active_engagements). The only currently-verified employer in the test dataset has hours_balance=0 and sits at index 25 in /api/employers response — so verified-badge-{empId} is never rendered on the talent dashboard. Code is correct; either (a) surface verified employers first, or (b) seed the verified test employer with some hours_balance for observable QA.
React hydration warning: <span> cannot be a child of <option>. Some source-map instrumentation wraps the {n} interpolation in a <span> inside <option>. Non-blocking but pollutes console.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix VerifyEmail.jsx to guard against double useEffect invocation under React.StrictMode (useRef flag) — currently every successful email verification is shown as 'Link expired' to the user.
MEDIUM: On TalentDashboard, either prioritize verified employers in the top-12 slice or seed the verified test employer with hours_balance>0 so the golden-star badge is actually visible.
LOW: Suppress hydration warning on cp-duration <option> mapping.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py register endpoint: swallows email-send exceptions silently — good for dev, but at minimum log the exception so real Resend errors don't disappear.

auth.py /verification/bgv: work_history validation says 'at least one' but the message-position order is: refs<2 checked before work<1, so a request with zero work + zero refs returns 'at least two references' — misleading; validate work_history first or use pydantic constraints.
server.py /employers: verified employers should be surfaced regardless of hours_balance — sorting by hours_balance hides freshly-verified employers.
VerifyEmail.jsx: not idempotent w/ React StrictMode — critical UX bug (see above).

auth.py /auth/register: does NOT block login for unverified users (intentional per spec) — banner-based ux, verified. But it also does NOT rate-limit /auth/resend-verification, so a user could rotate tokens indefinitely.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest file lives at /app/backend/tests/test_iteration26_verification.py (16 tests, all pass). It approves the employer + talent as part of the flow so any subsequent test that expects verification_status=pending on those accounts must reset them first (db.users.update_one). The VerifyEmail double-call StrictMode bug is deterministic in the preview build — reproducing it only requires visiting /verify-email?token=X once with a fresh token.
rca of the issue: VerifyEmail.jsx useEffect issues a network call synchronously on mount. Because /app/frontend/src/index.js wraps <App/> in <React.StrictMode>, React intentionally mounts the component twice in development-mode simulations to surface unsafe effects. Each mount fires the effect, so the server sees two GET /api/auth/verify-email?token=<X> requests. The first call succeeds and unsets the token; the second call finds no matching document and returns 400 -> UI transitions to state='fail'. Mitigation: gate the fetch with a useRef flag, e.g. `const ran = useRef(false); useEffect(() => { if (ran.current) return; ran.current = true; api.get(...) }, [params]);` — or use React 18's AbortController pattern to cancel the second call.
